case_name: L. O. v. Mt. Lebanon S.D.

issues.label: Standard of review of Board adjudication
issues.why: The court must determine whether it reviews for errors of law, constitutional violations, or lack of substantial evidence rather than reweighing facts.

issues.label: Scope of common pleas review authority
issues.why: Whether common pleas acted properly in reviewing on the existing record without taking additional evidence affects the applicable review standard.

issues.label: Legal definition of residency under Section 1302
issues.why: The court must interpret whether residency requires physical presence, domicile, or primary residence for school enrollment purposes.

issues.label: Physical presence versus domicile distinction
issues.why: Whether 10 of 36 nights suffices to establish residency turns on which legal standard governs.

issues.label: Allocation and shifting of burden of proof
issues.why: Whether Mother bore an initial burden that never shifted or the District carried the burden is dispositive of the outcome.

issues.label: Whether burden argument was waived
issues.why: The court must decide if the District preserved its burden-of-proof argument or raised it improperly for the first time on appeal.

issues.label: Whether multi-district residency argument waived
issues.why: Mother contends the District waived its argument that the ruling permits residency in multiple districts.

issues.label: Possibility of residency in multiple districts
issues.why: The court must decide whether Section 1302 permits a parent to reside in two or more districts simultaneously.

issues.label: Substantial evidence supporting non-residency finding
issues.why: The court must assess whether returned mail, low electric usage, and surveillance constitute substantial evidence of non-residency.

issues.label: Deference to Board credibility determinations
issues.why: Whether common pleas improperly rejected the Board's findings that Mother and Service Provider were not credible.

issues.label: Sufficiency of surveillance evidence
issues.why: The court must weigh whether limited two-day surveillance reasonably supports a non-residency conclusion.

issues.label: Weight of returned mail 'vacant' notation
issues.why: Whether the returned envelope's notation is probative given Mother's explanation about not updating the post office.

issues.label: Weight of minimal electric usage evidence
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether low kWh usage supports non-residency amid ongoing construction.

issues.label: Relevance of one-bedroom apartment adequacy
issues.why: Whether apartment size for four people is a legally proper factor in determining residency.

issues.label: Effect of intent versus actual residence
issues.why: The court must address whether Mother's stated desire to move was improperly conflated with actual residency.

issues.label: Relevant time period for residency determination
issues.why: Whether residency should be measured only October 20–November 26 or a broader window affects the analysis.

issues.label: Effect of unlivable conditions on presence
issues.why: Whether construction, illness, and utility outages excuse absences from the apartment for residency purposes.

issues.label: Scope of tuition liability for full year
issues.why: Whether imposing tuition for the entire 2024-25 year is supported absent findings about residency after the hearing.

issues.label: Compliance with District's 60-day notice policy
issues.why: Whether the District violated its own Residency/Enrollment Policy by acting before providing required notice.

issues.label: Judicial notice of District policy document
issues.why: Whether the notice provision is reviewable as a public record despite not being considered below.

issues.label: Denial of after-discovered evidence hearing
issues.why: Whether common pleas properly denied the District's motion to present video surveillance evidence.

issues.label: Acceptance of supplemental reproduced record
issues.why: Whether common pleas erred in accepting Mother's supplemental record after declaring the certified record complete.

issues.label: Relevance of estranged spouse/domestic violence context
issues.why: Whether Mother's inability to sell the Pittsburgh House and DV circumstances bear on residency determination.

issues.label: Effect of driver's license address
issues.why: Whether Mother's license listing the Pittsburgh House is dispositive or merely one factor in residency.

issues.label: Whether case involves separated parents
issues.why: The Board's finding that this is not a separated-parents case affects which residency rules apply.

issues.label: Proper remedy on appeal
issues.why: The court must decide whether to reinstate the Adjudication, affirm, or remand for further proceedings.
